name: Gossamer Delta
geological_features: An enormous river delta covering a quarter of the primary continent
Braided waterways threading through silt islands
Limestone karst formations riddled with sinkholes
Tidal marshlands along the continental shelf
specific_features: Silk-like filaments produced by delta-dwelling organisms that span between islands
description: Gossamer Delta is a water-rich terrestrial world where a single massive river system drains an entire continent into a delta of staggering proportions. Thousands of silt islands rise just above the waterline, connected by the gossamer filaments of colonial organisms that weave structures between them. The landscape is flat, green, and endlessly intricate.

Humidity saturates the air, and mornings bring fog so dense it obscures the horizon entirely. The gossamer threads catch moisture and sunlight alike, turning the delta into a shimmering lacework at midday. Bird-analogues wheel overhead in vast flocks, their calls echoing across the still water.

The colonial organisms that produce the gossamer filaments are unlike any cataloged species. They appear to function as a single distributed intelligence, responding collectively to environmental stimuli with remarkable coordination. Researchers debate whether this constitutes true sapience or merely an extraordinarily complex reflexive network.

Gossamer Delta's pharmaceutical potential is significant, as several delta organisms produce novel biochemical compounds. However, the ecological fragility of the delta system means any resource extraction must be carefully managed. The gossamer organisms, in particular, have become the subject of intense scientific and ethical debate regarding their cognitive status.
